weeks.title: Programme overview
weeks.content:
6-Week SPP Sprint Programme
World Athletics Level 3 coaching style • High-school athletes • 100 m and 200 m • No gym equipment
This programme is designed for your male and female sprint groups, with acceleration, maximum velocity, speed endurance, sprint mechanics, bodyweight strength and core training. It follows a six-week Specific Preparation Phase (SPP) approach, moving from specific speed development towards race-specific work.
The programme uses a Monday–Saturday schedule, with Thursday and Sunday as rest days. Since this is for high-school athletes, the target times are training guides, not guarantees of future personal bests.
1. Athlete groups and performance targets
Male sprinters
Athlete A — current PB
11.08 / 22.68
100 m / 200 m
Target PB
10.60 / 21.80
100 m / 200 m
Athlete B — current PB
11.30 / 23.36
100 m / 200 m
Target PB
10.60 / 21.80
100 m / 200 m
Both males follow the same sessions but use individual targets. Athlete B should generally start at the more conservative end of the intensity range.
Female sprinters
Current PB
13.00 / 27.00
100 m / 200 m
Target PB
12.40 / 24.80
100 m / 200 m
Female athletes use the same weekly structure, with their own target times and reductions in volume whenever technique or recovery deteriorates.
2. Important coaching rules
Warm-up: 15–20 minutes before every track session.
Sprint quality: Fast repetitions must remain technically sound. Stop a speed set if times slow by around 3% or more, or mechanics visibly deteriorate.
Rest: Full recovery for acceleration and maximum-speed work; shorter recoveries are reserved for controlled tempo running.
Strength: Monday and Saturday, using bodyweight only.
Spikes: Introduce gradually for selected fast sessions, rather than every day.
Sleds: This plan is equipment-free, so no sled is required. If you have access to a sled, use light resisted accelerations as an optional replacement for some Monday starts, not an additional workload.
Recovery: Thursday and Sunday are rest days. Easy mobility or walking is optional.
A 10.60-second 100 m and a 21.80-second 200 m are ambitious goals, especially within one six-week block. The purpose of this SPP is to build the specific speed qualities needed to progress towards those targets, not to promise those times by Week 6.
3. Standard warm-up for every track session
Stage 1 — Raise temperature
Easy jog: 3–4 minutes
Rest: 30 seconds
Ankle bounces: 2 × 15
Stage 2 — Dynamic mobility
Walking lunges: 2 × 10 m
Leg swings: 10 per leg
A-march: 2 × 20 m
Rest: 30 seconds between drills
Stage 3 — Sprint preparation
A-skips: 2 × 20 m
High knees: 2 × 20 m
Straight-leg runs: 2 × 20 m
Rest: 45–60 seconds
Stage 4 — Progressive strides
3 × 40 m at approximately 60%, 70% and 80%
Walk back, then rest until fully ready
Rest 2 minutes before the main session
For maximum-velocity sessions, add one or two progressive runs before the first fast repetition. For sessions involving spikes, perform most of the warm-up in trainers.
4. Target-time guide
These are initial coaching ranges, not official World Athletics standards. They assume a reasonably flat, measured track and hand timing. Electronic timing, wind, surface and starting method will affect results.

TABLE  •  20 m acceleration  |  3.0–3.3 s  |  3.1–3.4 s  |  3.4–3.8 s
TABLE  •  30 m acceleration  |  4.0–4.3 s  |  4.1–4.4 s  |  4.5–4.9 s
TABLE  •  Flying 20 m  |  2.05–2.20 s  |  2.10–2.25 s  |  2.30–2.50 s
TABLE  •  Flying 30 m  |  3.05–3.25 s  |  3.10–3.30 s  |  3.45–3.70 s
TABLE  •  60 m from blocks  |  7.2–7.6 s  |  7.3–7.8 s  |  8.0–8.6 s
TABLE  •  80 m fast but relaxed  |  9.0–9.5 s  |  9.2–9.7 s  |  10.3–11.0 s
TABLE  •  120 m speed endurance  |  13.8–14.8 s  |  14.1–15.1 s  |  15.8–17.0 s
TABLE  •  150 m speed endurance  |  17.0–18.2 s  |  17.4–18.7 s  |  19.5–21.0 s
Important: Flying-run times refer to the flying segment only, after a gradual build-up. The 60 m targets are starting estimates and must be checked against actual testing. Do not force an athlete to hit a target by straining or overstriding.
For the 100 m and 200 m race-distance repetitions later in the plan, use the session-specific targets below rather than treating every rep as an all-out race.
5. Six-week day-by-day SPP programme

weeks.title: Week 1 — Establish specific speed
weeks.content:
Week 1 — Establish specific speed
Focus: acceleration, sprint posture, relaxed maximum velocity and introductory speed endurance.
Monday — Acceleration + strength
Speed + strength
4 × 20 m from a standing or three-point start.
3 × 30 m from a three-point start.
Male targets: 20 m in 3.0–3.4 s; 30 m in 4.0–4.4 s.
Female targets: 20 m in 3.4–3.8 s; 30 m in 4.5–4.9 s.
Rest: 2 minutes after 20 m, 3 minutes after 30 m.
Bodyweight strength: 2 rounds of 8 squats, 8 reverse lunges per leg, 10 glute bridges, 8 push-ups and 20-second front plank.
Rest 45–60 seconds between exercises.
Tuesday — Tempo + core
6 × 100 m at 65–70%, on grass or track.
Guide: males 15.0–17.0 s; females 17.0–19.0 s.
Rest: 60–75 seconds.
Core: dead bug 2 × 8 per side, side plank 2 × 20 seconds per side, bird dog 2 × 8 per side.
Rest 30–45 seconds between exercises.
Wednesday — Introductory speed endurance
3 × 120 m at 85–90%, relaxed and technically controlled.
Guide: Male A 15.0–16.0 s; Male B 15.3–16.3 s; females 17.0–18.2 s.
Rest: 6–8 minutes.
Finish with 2 × 60 m relaxed strides at 70%, resting 2 minutes.
No additional strength work.
Thursday — Rest
Complete rest from structured sprint training. Optional gentle walking or mobility.
Friday — Maximum velocity
4 × flying 20 m, with a 20–25 m progressive run-in.
Guide: males 2.05–2.25 s; females 2.30–2.50 s.
Rest: 4–5 minutes between reps.
2 × 60 m at 90–95%, males approximately 7.5–8.2 s; females 8.5–9.3 s.
Rest: 4 minutes.
Use spikes for the final 2 flying reps only if the athlete is accustomed to them.
Saturday — Tempo + strength and core
5 × 100 m at 65–70%.
Guide: males 15.0–17.0 s; females 17.0–19.0 s.
Rest: 60–75 seconds.
Strength: 2 rounds of 10 squats, 8 split squats per leg, 12 calf raises, 8 push-ups.
Core: 2 × 25-second plank and 2 × 20-second side plank per side.
Rest 45–60 seconds between exercises.

weeks.title: Week 2 — Improve acceleration and speed exposure
weeks.content:
Week 2 — Improve acceleration and speed exposure
Increase the quality of the fast running, not the amount of exhaustion.
Monday — Acceleration + strength
4 × 20 m starts.
4 × 30 m starts.
Targets: use Week 1 ranges; aim for consistent or slightly faster technically sound runs.
Rest: 2 minutes for 20 m, 3 minutes for 30 m.
Strength: 2 rounds of 10 squats, 8 reverse lunges per leg, 10 glute bridges, 8–10 push-ups and 25-second plank.
Tuesday — Tempo + core
7 × 100 m at 65–70%.
Males: 15.0–17.0 s; females: 17.0–19.0 s.
Rest: 60–75 seconds.
Core: dead bug 2 × 10 per side, side plank 2 × 25 seconds per side, bird dog 2 × 10 per side.
Wednesday — Speed endurance
3 × 150 m at 85–90%.
Male A: 18.0–19.0 s; Male B: 18.3–19.3 s; females: 20.5–22.0 s.
Rest: 7–8 minutes.
Finish with 2 × 60 m relaxed strides, resting 2 minutes.
Thursday — Rest
Friday — Maximum velocity
4 × flying 20 m, using a 20–25 m run-in.
Male A: 2.05–2.20 s; Male B: 2.10–2.25 s; females: 2.30–2.50 s.
Rest: 4–5 minutes.
2 × 60 m at 90–95%; rest 4 minutes.
Spikes: final 2 flying reps if appropriate.
Saturday — Tempo + strength
5 × 120 m at 65–70%.
Males: approximately 18.0–20.0 s; females: 20.5–22.5 s.
Rest: 75 seconds.
Strength: 2 rounds of 10 squats, 8 split squats per leg, 12 calf raises and 8 push-ups.
Core: 2 × 30-second plank and 2 × 25-second side plank per side.

weeks.title: Week 3 — Transition to more specific sprinting
weeks.content:
Week 3 — Transition to more specific sprinting
Focus: faster flying runs, longer acceleration and race-relevant speed endurance.
Monday — Acceleration + strength
3 × 20 m starts.
4 × 30 m starts.
2 × 40 m accelerations.
Targets: use the Week 1–2 acceleration ranges for 20 and 30 m. For 40 m, aim for approximately 5.0–5.6 s for males and 5.7–6.3 s for females, then calibrate using actual results.
Rest: 2 minutes after 20 m; 3 minutes after 30 m; 4 minutes after 40 m.
Strength: 2 rounds of 10 squats, 8 split squats per leg, 10 glute bridges, 8 push-ups and 25-second plank.
Tuesday — Tempo + core
6 × 120 m at 65–70%.
Males: 18.0–20.0 s; females: 20.5–22.5 s.
Rest: 75 seconds.
Core: dead bug 2 × 10 per side, bird dog 2 × 10 per side, side plank 2 × 25 seconds per side.
Wednesday — Speed endurance
2 × 150 m at 90–92%.
Male A: 17.0–18.0 s; Male B: 17.4–18.5 s; females: 19.5–21.0 s.
Rest: 8–10 minutes.
Then 1 × 100 m at 90%, maintaining relaxation. Use approximately 12.0–12.8 s for males and 14.0–15.0 s for females as an initial guide.
Rest before the 100 m: 8 minutes.
Thursday — Rest
Friday — Maximum velocity + spikes
4 × flying 30 m with a 25–30 m build-up.
Male A: 3.05–3.25 s; Male B: 3.10–3.30 s; females: 3.45–3.70 s.
Rest: 5–6 minutes.
2 × 60 m at 90–95%, resting 4 minutes.
Spikes may be used for 2–4 quality repetitions if the athlete is adapted to them.
Saturday — Tempo + strength and core
4 × 100 m at 65–70%, resting 60–75 seconds.
Strength: 2 rounds of 10 squats, 8 reverse lunges per leg, 12 calf raises and 8 push-ups.
Core: 2 × 30-second front plank, 2 × 25-second side plank per side.

weeks.title: Week 4 — Race-specific speed endurance
weeks.content:
Week 4 — Race-specific speed endurance
This is the main loading week. Maintain full recovery on high-intensity days.
Monday — Starts + acceleration strength
4 × 20 m starts.
3 × 30 m starts.
2 × 40 m accelerations.
Rest: 2, 3 and 4 minutes respectively.
Strength: 2 rounds of 8 squats, 8 split squats per leg, 10 glute bridges, 8 push-ups and 25-second plank.
Tuesday — Tempo + core
6 × 100 m at 65–70%.
Males: 15.0–17.0 s; females: 17.0–19.0 s.
Rest: 60–75 seconds.
Core: dead bug 2 × 10 per side, bird dog 2 × 10 per side, side plank 2 × 30 seconds per side.
Wednesday — 200 m speed endurance
2 × 180 m at 90–92%, with even pacing and no sprinting beyond technical control.
Male A: approximately 21.5–23.0 s; Male B: 22.0–23.5 s; females: 25.0–27.0 s.
Rest: 10–12 minutes.
If the first repetition is slower than expected or form breaks down, stop after one quality repetition rather than forcing the second.
Thursday — Rest
Friday — Maximum velocity
3 × flying 30 m.
Targets: males 3.05–3.30 s; females 3.45–3.70 s.
Rest: 5–6 minutes.
2 × 80 m at 90–95%, resting 5 minutes.
Guide for 80 m: males 9.0–9.7 s; females 10.3–11.0 s.
Spikes: optional for flying runs and the first 80 m if the athlete is accustomed to them.
Saturday — Recovery tempo + strength
4 × 100 m at 60–65%, resting 75 seconds.
Strength: 2 rounds of 8 squats, 8 lunges per leg, 10 glute bridges, 8 push-ups and 12 calf raises.
Core: front plank 2 × 25 seconds and side plank 2 × 20 seconds per side.

weeks.title: Week 5 — Highest specificity, controlled volume
weeks.content:
Week 5 — Highest specificity, controlled volume
Keep the fast work high quality while reducing unnecessary repetitions.
Monday — Acceleration + strength
3 × 20 m starts.
3 × 30 m starts.
2 × 40 m accelerations.
Rest: 2, 3 and 4 minutes respectively.
Strength: 2 rounds of 8 squats, 8 split squats per leg, 10 glute bridges, 8 push-ups and 25-second plank.
Tuesday — Tempo + core
5 × 100 m at 65–70%.
Males: 15.0–17.0 s; females: 17.0–19.0 s.
Rest: 60–75 seconds.
Core: dead bug 2 × 10 per side, bird dog 2 × 8 per side and side plank 2 × 25 seconds per side.
Wednesday — Race-specific speed endurance
1 × 150 m at 92–95%.
Male A: 16.8–17.8 s; Male B: 17.2–18.2 s; females: 19.3–20.5 s.
Rest: 10 minutes.
1 × 120 m at approximately 90%.
Male A: 14.0–14.8 s; Male B: 14.3–15.1 s; females: 16.0–17.0 s.
No extra repetitions if the athlete struggles to maintain mechanics.
Thursday — Rest
Friday — Maximum velocity + spikes
3 × flying 30 m, resting 5–6 minutes.
Male A: 3.05–3.25 s; Male B: 3.10–3.30 s; females: 3.45–3.70 s.
1 × 80 m at 95% with relaxed mechanics; rest 5–6 minutes before it.
Spikes may be used for the flying runs and 80 m if fully adapted.
Saturday — Light tempo + core
4 × 100 m at 60–65%, resting 75 seconds.
Bodyweight strength: 1–2 rounds of 8 squats, 8 lunges per leg, 10 glute bridges and 8 push-ups.
Core: 2 × 25-second plank and 2 × 20-second side plank per side.

weeks.title: Week 6 — Consolidation and testing
weeks.content:
Week 6 — Consolidation and testing
Reduce volume, retain speed and assess readiness for the next phase.
Monday — Acceleration + light strength
3 × 20 m starts.
3 × 30 m starts.
Rest: 2–3 minutes.
Strength: 1–2 rounds of 8 squats, 6 lunges per leg, 10 glute bridges and 8 push-ups.
Core: 2 × 20-second plank.
Tuesday — Easy tempo + mobility
4 × 100 m at 60–65%.
Males: approximately 16.0–18.0 s; females: 18.0–20.0 s.
Rest: 75 seconds.
Light mobility and relaxed drills. No demanding core session.
Wednesday — Speed assessment
3 × 30 m from the same start position used in earlier testing.
Rest: 4 minutes.
2 × flying 20 m with a consistent run-in.
Rest: 5 minutes.
Record the best technically sound time, not just the fastest time.
Use the Week 1 test results for comparison.
Thursday — Rest
Friday — Optional 100 m or 200 m race-model session
Choose only one option, based on the athlete's primary event and readiness.
100 m group: 1 × 80 m at 95%, with 6–8 minutes of recovery after the warm-up.
200 m group: 1 × 120 m at 90–95%, followed by full recovery.
Male 120 m guide: 13.8–14.8 s; female guide: 15.8–17.0 s.
If testing on Wednesday caused fatigue, replace this session with 4 × 60 m relaxed strides at 70%, resting 2 minutes.
Saturday — Light strength + mobility
2 × 8 bodyweight squats.
2 × 8 glute bridges.
2 × 8 push-ups or an easier variation.
2 × 20-second front plank.
10 minutes of gentle mobility.
No maximal sprinting.
Sunday — Rest
6. When to use spikes

weeks.title: Weeks 1–2
weeks.content:
Weeks 1–2
Use trainers for acceleration and most running. If athletes are already adapted to spikes, introduce them for only 2–4 flying repetitions on Friday.

weeks.title: Weeks 3–4
weeks.content:
Weeks 3–4
Use spikes for selected Friday maximum-velocity repetitions. Start with a small number of reps and avoid changing footwear and sprint volume aggressively at the same time.

weeks.title: Weeks 5–6
weeks.content:
Weeks 5–6
Use spikes for selected high-quality sprinting or testing, provided athletes have no foot, calf, Achilles or hamstring symptoms. Trainers remain suitable for all tempo sessions.
7. Sled work — optional, not required
Because you requested a programme without equipment, the main programme does not depend on sleds. If a sled becomes available, use it on Monday in place of some acceleration repetitions:
3 × 15 m light sled accelerations.
Rest 2–3 minutes.
Use a load that allows the athlete to maintain sprint posture and near-normal acceleration mechanics.
Remove 2–3 unresisted starts when adding sled work; do not simply add the sled reps to the existing session.
For school athletes, avoid heavy resisted sprinting that substantially changes running mechanics. Never use improvised loads that cannot be controlled safely.
8. Coaching and progression checklist
Use this checklist every week to decide whether to progress the athlete.

weeks.title: Weekly coaching review
weeks.content:
Weekly coaching review
0 of 5
Acceleration
Pushes backward, projects forward and rises gradually.
Maximum velocity
Tall hips, relaxed shoulders, stable posture and active ground contact.
Speed endurance
Maintains rhythm without reaching or collapsing late in the rep.
Recovery
No persistent hamstring, groin, calf, Achilles or knee pain.
Timing
Distances and start methods remain consistent across testing.
Reset checklist
Final coaching recommendation
For your athletes, the most important sessions are Monday's acceleration, Wednesday's speed endurance and Friday's maximum velocity. Protect the quality of these sessions by keeping Tuesday and Saturday controlled and by enforcing the Thursday and Sunday rest days.
Do not judge success solely by whether athletes reach 10.60, 21.80 or 12.40 in six weeks. Judge it by improvements in acceleration, flying-run times, technical consistency, speed endurance and recovery. Reassess their personal bests after the block and use the results to design the next phase.

Week 4 — Race-specific speed endurance
This is the main loading week. Maintain full recovery on high-intensity days.
Monday — Starts + acceleration strength

3 × 30 m starts.

Wednesday — 200 m speed endurance

Male A: approximately 21.5–23.0 s; Male B: 22.0–23.5 s; females: 25.0–27.0 s.
Rest: 10–12 minutes.
If the first repetition is slower than expected or form breaks down, stop after one quality repetition rather than forcing the second.
Thursday — Rest
Friday — Maximum velocity

Targets: males 3.05–3.30 s; females 3.45–3.70 s.
Rest: 5–6 minutes.
2 × 80 m at 90–95%, resting 5 minutes.

Spikes: optional for flying runs and the first 80 m if the athlete is accustomed to them.
Saturday — Recovery tempo + strength
4 × 100 m at 60–65%, resting 75 seconds.
Strength: 2 rounds of 8 squats, 8 lunges per leg, 10 glute bridges, 8 push-ups and 12 calf raises.
Core: front plank 2 × 25 seconds and side plank 2 × 20 seconds per side.
Week 5 — Highest specificity, controlled volume
Keep the fast work high quality while reducing unnecessary repetitions.
Monday — Acceleration + strength
3 × 20 m starts.
3 × 30 m starts.
2 × 40 m accelerations.
Rest: 2, 3 and 4 minutes respectively.
Strength: 2 rounds of 8 squats, 8 split squats per leg, 10 glute bridges, 8 push-ups and 25-second plank.

Wednesday — Race-specific speed endurance
1 × 150 m at 92–95%.
Male A: 16.8–17.8 s; Male B: 17.2–18.2 s; females: 19.3–20.5 s.
Rest: 10 minutes.

Male A: 14.0–14.8 s; Male B: 14.3–15.1 s; females: 16.0–17.0 s.
No extra repetitions if the athlete struggles to maintain mechanics.
Thursday — Rest
Friday — Maximum velocity + spikes

Male A: 3.05–3.25 s; Male B: 3.10–3.30 s; females: 3.45–3.70 s.
1 × 80 m at 95% with relaxed mechanics; rest 5–6 minutes before it.
Spikes may be used for the flying runs and 80 m if fully adapted.
Saturday — Light tempo + core
4 × 100 m at 60–65%, resting 75 seconds.
Bodyweight strength: 1–2 rounds of 8 squats, 8 lunges per leg, 10 glute bridges and 8 push-ups.
Core: 2 × 25-second plank and 2 × 20-second side plank per side.
Week 6 — Consolidation and testing
Reduce volume, retain speed and assess readiness for the next phase.
Monday — Acceleration + light strength
3 × 20 m starts.
3 × 30 m starts.
Rest: 2–3 minutes.
Strength: 1–2 rounds of 8 squats, 6 lunges per leg, 10 glute bridges and 8 push-ups.
Core: 2 × 20-second plank.
Tuesday — Easy tempo + mobility
4 × 100 m at 60–65%.
Males: approximately 16.0–18.0 s; females: 18.0–20.0 s.
Rest: 75 seconds.
Light mobility and relaxed drills. No demanding core session.
Wednesday — Speed assessment
3 × 30 m from the same start position used in earlier testing.
Rest: 4 minutes.
2 × flying 20 m with a consistent run-in.
Rest: 5 minutes.
Record the best technically sound time, not just the fastest time.
Use the Week 1 test results for comparison.
Thursday — Rest
Friday — Optional 100 m or 200 m race-model session
Choose only one option, based on the athlete's primary event and readiness.
100 m group: 1 × 80 m at 95%, with 6–8 minutes of recovery after the warm-up.
200 m group: 1 × 120 m at 90–95%, followed by full recovery.
Male 120 m guide: 13.8–14.8 s; female guide: 15.8–17.0 s.
If testing on Wednesday caused fatigue, replace this session with 4 × 60 m relaxed strides at 70%, resting 2 minutes.
Saturday — Light strength + mobility
2 × 8 bodyweight squats.
2 × 8 glute bridges.
2 × 8 push-ups or an easier variation.
2 × 20-second front plank.
10 minutes of gentle mobility.
No maximal sprinting.
Sunday — Rest
6. When to use spikes
Weeks 1–2
Use trainers for acceleration and most running. If athletes are already adapted to spikes, introduce them for only 2–4 flying repetitions on Friday.
Weeks 3–4
Use spikes for selected Friday maximum-velocity repetitions. Start with a small number of reps and avoid changing footwear and sprint volume aggressively at the same time.
Weeks 5–6
Use spikes for selected high-quality sprinting or testing, provided athletes have no foot, calf, Achilles or hamstring symptoms. Trainers remain suitable for all tempo sessions.
7. Sled work — optional, not required
Because you requested a programme without equipment, the main programme does not depend on sleds. If a sled becomes available, use it on Monday in place of some acceleration repetitions:
3 × 15 m light sled accelerations.
Rest 2–3 minutes.
Use a load that allows the athlete to maintain sprint posture and near-normal acceleration mechanics.
Remove 2–3 unresisted starts when adding sled work; do not simply add the sled reps to the existing session.
For school athletes, avoid heavy resisted sprinting that substantially changes running mechanics. Never use improvised loads that cannot be controlled safely.
8. Coaching and progression checklist
Use this checklist every week to decide whether to progress the athlete.
Weekly coaching review
0 of 5
Acceleration
Pushes backward, projects forward and rises gradually.
Maximum velocity
Tall hips, relaxed shoulders, stable posture and active ground contact.
Speed endurance
Maintains rhythm without reaching or collapsing late in the rep.
Recovery
No persistent hamstring, groin, calf, Achilles or knee pain.
Timing
Distances and start methods remain consistent across testing.
Reset checklist
Final coaching recommendation
For your athletes, the most important sessions are Monday's acceleration, Wednesday's speed endurance and Friday's maximum velocity. Protect the quality of these sessions by keeping Tuesday and Saturday controlled and by enforcing the Thursday and Sunday rest days.
Do not judge success solely by whether athletes reach 10.60, 21.80 or 12.40 in six weeks. Judge it by improvements in acceleration, flying-run times, technical consistency, speed endurance and recovery. Reassess their personal bests after the block and use the results to design the next phase.

Below is an 8-week advanced GPP sprint program structured in a World Athletics Level 4-style performance model for high-school sprinters. It is designed around a traditional progression from general capacity → acceleration → maximum velocity → speed endurance → pre-SPP preparation.

Female target: 12.00–11.70 / 23.00–22.99

COACHING RULES
1. Speed comes before conditioning
If an athlete is running a speed session, do not turn it into conditioning.
Once sprint times deteriorate by approximately 3% or more, stop the high-quality sprint component.
2. Full recovery for maximum velocity
Maximum-velocity work requires:
4–6 min recovery for flying sprints
6–8 min for 60m high-quality efforts
The purpose is quality, not fatigue.
3. Sleds are acceleration tools
Do not use heavy sleds simply to make athletes tired.
The athlete should still demonstrate:
stable trunk
aggressive projection
positive shin angles
powerful hip extension
rhythmic arm action
4. Hills are not maximal races
Athletes should run aggressively while maintaining mechanics.
Avoid:
excessive forward bending
overstriding
collapsing at the hips
grinding through the final 20m
5. Female athletes
Do not automatically give female athletes lower-quality training because their absolute times are slower. The same training principles apply, but sprint distances, target velocities and recovery should be individualized.
6. Progression
The 8-week progression should move from:
General capacity → acceleration strength → acceleration → maximum velocity → speed endurance → specific preparation readiness.
GPP EXIT CRITERIA
Before moving into SPP, athletes should demonstrate:
Acceleration
Consistent 10–30m acceleration
Stable projection mechanics
No major technique breakdown
Maximum velocity
Ability to sprint at high velocity without excessive tension
Consistent flying-sprint times
Speed endurance
Ability to maintain mechanics during 100–180m work
Controlled relaxation under fatigue
General strength
Good unilateral leg control

Important coaching adjustment
For high-school athletes, do not require every athlete to hit the listed target times simply because those are the desired end goals. Also, for athletes racing frequently, the race itself replaces the Friday high-intensity session rather than being added on top of it. This is especially important during Weeks 9–12.

2 × 30 m accelerations.

Race the primary event: 100 m or 200 m.

Final coaching guidance
For your athletes, the most important principle during CP and peaking is quality over quantity. Avoid stacking maximal speed endurance, flying sprints and competitions on consecutive days. A competition replaces the hard session scheduled for that day; it is not an addition to it.
Use actual competition results to assess progress towards 10.60/21.80 for the males and 12.40/24.80 for the females. Those goals may require further development beyond this eight-week block. The best peak is one where athletes arrive healthy, confident, technically prepared and ready to express their speed.
